fences.title: Readers load published objects and portraits from img.brinedew.bio
fences.decision: Readers load the published Iconoplasm objects (genes/v3/<SYMBOL>.json, catalog/v3/index.json) and the immutable portrait bytes from img.brinedew.bio, Cloudflare's free cache in front of the Bunny pull zone (B-1087). The site rewrites every delivered image URL onto that host and runs no probe or Worker fallback. The extension keeps its probe and fallback until its next store release. First-party identity remains canonical.
fences.reason: Repeat views should cost neither the Worker allowance nor Bunny bandwidth. The old probe and fallback existed because some ISP resolvers could not resolve *.b-cdn.net; img.brinedew.bio resolves through Cloudflare like the site itself, and a fallback only moved images onto metered Worker requests.
fences.change_control: A replacement must preserve byte identity and keep repeat reads off the Worker and off Bunny's bill. Implementation details may change without preserving the old mechanism.

fences.title: Gene discovery is eligibility-gated and built from the catalog object
fences.decision: One stable gene object defines each gene's public identity, from which its blot's address follows, and one catalog object defines the discoverable set. Complete profiles are discoverable; incomplete or inconsistent publication fails closed and never repairs itself on a reader request.
fences.reason: Search, archives, metadata, and images must agree without making public readers perform authoring work.
fences.change_control: A replacement must keep one eligibility rule and one public image identity across every surface. Rendering, indexing, storage, and sitemap mechanics may change.

fences.title: Scheduled wakeups follow durable due times
fences.decision: Scheduled wakeups run durable due work; they are not polling tokens. Repeated dirty work is coalesced. Batch work is let in by its price before it spends shared capacity (IPD-013).
fences.reason: Blind retries and one-message-per-event designs can exhaust queues and databases without producing user value.
fences.change_control: A replacement must preserve durable intent, idempotency and bounded idle cost. Schedules and batch sizes may change.

fences.title: The primary Iconoplasm D1 is bounded operational state
fences.decision: The primary Iconoplasm D1 stores bounded operational state. Large immutable bodies and retained history use appropriate separate storage and explicit retention.
fences.reason: Unbounded history or duplicated payloads can fill the mutation database and stop unrelated user actions.
fences.change_control: A replacement must prove bounded growth, recoverability, and truthful capacity reporting. Tables, thresholds, retention periods, and storage layout may change.

fences.title: Fulfillment is one bounded receipt per reader order, recipient, and gene
fences.decision: One reader order (request_batch_id) has one durable fulfillment receipt per recipient and gene, whichever Drain sessions finish its requests. Cancelled requests leave the group. Notifications and inbox state derive from that receipt.
fences.reason: Timing and row adjacency cannot reliably identify a complete human-visible result.
fences.change_control: A replacement must preserve group completeness, idempotency, bounded payloads, and one acknowledgement boundary. Presentation and delivery mechanisms may change.

fences.title: Iconoplasm is static-first with one dynamic Worker invocation
fences.decision: Anonymous Iconoplasm documents are static and healthy portrait reads go directly to Bunny. The stable first-party /blot/{symbol}.webp route uses the one existing Worker to resolve the exact stable gene object and its immutable image. Canonical /portraits/* URLs use that Worker for a real Bunny-backed fallback; private actions, mutations, and administration use the same Worker.
fences.reason: Public reading must scale without a metered Worker invocation for every healthy asset or page. The canonical fallback must deliver actual image bytes, and a mutable blot URL must not serve stale or mislabeled bytes after the stable gene object changes.
fences.change_control: Keep the shell static, healthy portrait delivery direct from Bunny, the canonical portrait fallback byte-correct, and the stable blot route tied to the exact stable gene object. A replacement must preserve complete public reading and bound Worker use to routes that actually need it. Routing, caching, and deployment mechanics may change.

fences.title: Anonymous startup and extension hover use the published read plane
fences.decision: Anonymous startup and extension hover read the two published objects (the stable gene object from the CDN and the catalog object) with bounded local reuse. They do not probe private identity, scan mutable state, or repair publication.
fences.reason: Reading should remain fast and available without coupling every page or hover to authentication and database capacity.
fences.change_control: A replacement must preserve one published authority, independent portrait and detail progress, bounded caches, and zero mutable-state fallback for anonymous reads. Client scheduling and transport may change.

fences.title: Iconoplasm public reads stay cold-safe inside the one loud state boundary
fences.decision: Anonymous gene documents resolve one publisher's coherent static release. The stable first-party blot route and every other gene reader read the one stable gene object (genes/v3/<SYMBOL>.json) through the existing Worker. Anonymous reads never reconstruct public truth from D1, Durable Objects, Queues, sessions, or a second state owner.
fences.reason: A static published read plane keeps failures and traffic away from the mutation authority.
fences.change_control: A replacement must preserve one publisher, coherent fallback, and separation between public reads and mutable state. File names, manifests, object layout, and service topology may change.

fences.title: Routine publication is per gene and bounded
fences.decision: Routine publication rewrites one stable gene object per changed gene (about five subrequests, no Durable Object) and rebuilds the one catalog object outside the Worker in GitHub Actions. It never rebuilds the corpus inside a Worker request or cron tick.
fences.reason: Small user changes must not trigger work proportional to every published gene.
fences.change_control: A replacement must prove work is bounded by changed genes and that the catalog rebuild stays off the Worker. Object layout and schedule may change.

fences.title: Every public blot follows from the one stable gene object
fences.decision: The stable gene object owns the public character, current portrait and complete candidate pool for a gene, and the gene's blot address is computed from it alone (workers/lib/iconoplasm-blot.js); the catalog object carries the same portrait identity for the whole set. Every public surface resolves that same identity.
fences.reason: Separate portrait, metadata, and page authorities create split canon that readers cannot reason about.
fences.change_control: A replacement must preserve one committed identity per gene, verified bytes, and agreement across site, extension, APIs, metadata, and media. Storage and publication formats may change.

fences.title: Batch work is let in by its price, before it runs
fences.decision: Every Iconoplasm admin and workstation route names its D1 price: the Hono routes in app.js, the legacy gateway's routes in workers/iconoplasm/batch-route-prices.js, which refuses to load while a contract route of those audiences has no entry. A batch request is admitted only when Cloudflare's own meter total, plus the batch work admitted since the meter's newest minute, plus its price fit under the tier table's batch stop; a multi-page job prices its whole length on its first page; an unreadable meter stops batch work. Readers' own actions run to Cloudflare's wall. The app refuses to build when an admin route carries no price.
fences.reason: Cloudflare's usage meter runs one to two minutes late. On 2026-10-11 a copy wrote 62,000 rows in four minutes past an 85% stop that only read the meter, and readers lost their votes until 00:00 UTC. It was about the tenth outage of the same shape: work admitted before its price was known, guarded by a lagging signal.
fences.change_control: A replacement must keep admission before spend, count spend the meter has not shown yet, fail closed for batch work when the meter is unreadable, and read only Cloudflare's own meter (no private bank, Durable Object or quota). Prices, table layout and route names may change.

fences.title: Daily targets give every gene surname one slot
fences.decision: Automatic GeneGuessr selection gives each normalized gene surname one slot in a deterministic without-replacement cycle.
fences.reason: Rows and aliases must not multiply a family's lottery weight.
fences.change_control: A replacement must preserve one slot per surname and deterministic replay. Pool storage and selection implementation may change.

fences.title: Recap images require pixel and storage proof
fences.decision: A GeneGuessr recap image is publishable only after visible molecule pixels are ready and storage returns the exact uploaded bytes.
fences.reason: A successful request or attachment placeholder does not prove a usable recap image exists.
fences.change_control: A replacement must preserve pixel readiness, immutable identity, exact read-back, resumability, and text-only fallback. Renderer and storage mechanics may change.
